rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every chunk in order. Chunk 2 line 12 'The first bug fix here' and chunk 3 lines 18-19 'the bug'/'the bug's ticket' resolve via the check_slides.md §1 session-artifact carve-out ('the bug from prework' is explicitly listed exempt). Chunk 7 line 57 'the loop' resolves back to chunk 3 line 16's 'orient → fix → close → compound loop'. Chunk 8 line 66 'before it' resolves via its own header 'Pre-reads before Module 2' (header counts as in-chunk). No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

grep -n 'said\|earlier lecture\|opening lecture' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md returned no matches. Chunk 8's external readings are named by title/author, not by position ('The agentic engineering progression', Dex Horthy 'Why Software Factories Fail', Boris Cherny video, 'Multi-session and Git' reference). Chunk 9's 'Module 2' reference is a forward navigational name, not a positional callback into another file.

rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is M1 (line 3: 'Run M1 on high thinking effort'), the training's first module — there is no prior module for a backward 'the X you did/saw' construction to point at, and grep -n 'you did\|you saw\|you caught\|you ran' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md found no such body construction. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n 'guess\|predict' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md found no matches in the body (above the maintainer cut at line 79). No guess-before-reveal beat is present in this module file to check ordering on.

All 9 numbered chunks carry a self-standing claim or content block (Big Idea's thesis, Prework's instructions, the 5-item LO list, the 3 room norms, the 5 pacing bullets, the Start-here question + link list, the 5 Key Concepts, the 4-item reading list, the Next bridge paragraph). None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Checked each header against its chunk content: 'Big Idea' -> one-sentence thesis; 'Prework' -> prework instructions; 'What You'll Learn' -> 5 Bloom-verb LOs; 'How we work in this room' -> 3 room norms; 'Freedom to choose' -> pacing/flexibility bullets; 'Start here' -> the opening question + module link list; 'Key Concepts' -> 5 concept bullets; 'Pre-reads before Module 2' -> 4 optional readings; 'Next' -> Module 2 preview. Every header is a literally true summary of its chunk.

Sub-items checked per chunk: 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction — chunk 5 line 30 'Not too fast, not too slow' is a two-part idiom following its own declarative, not the banned three-part Not/Not/Z shape; not flagged. Anaphora/epistrophe triples — none found. Self-grading superlatives — none found (chunk 8 line 74's 'his single biggest productivity unlock' is Cherny's own attributed claim about worktrees, not the training grading itself). Number + own retraction — none found. Abstraction-noun stacks — none found (line 6 'compounding' and line 59 'the artifact rules' are single taught/plain terms, not stacked abstractions). Verb triplets with an empty leg — none found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -in 'surface\|firing\|compendium\|forcing function\|\bbeat\b\|\bmood\b\|Connections' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md against the body (lines 1-78) found no matches — the only hits are in the maintainer block (lines 83-125), which is out of scope for this rule. 'Compound' (line 6, 20, etc.) is the training's own taught vocabulary (Compound Engineering / the compound-and-close exercise), not repo-authorial dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: §9 exists to keep a projected, spoken-over slide from drowning its one real handle in decorative bold. Chunk 3 'What You'll Learn' (lines 16-20) bolds a lead word on all 5 bullets (**Run**, **Distinguish**, **Fix**, **Close**, **Compound**); chunk 4 'How we work in this room' (lines 24-26) bolds a lead phrase on all 3 bullets (**All learners.**, **Exercises.**, **Share and discuss.**). Per maintainer block line 99, chunk 4 is explicitly a live cohort-projected slide the trainer talks over before the trick-share — the exact scenario the budget targets. Neither chunk is a law/consolidation slide (no named laws/governors) and neither matches the 2026-08-13 reading-list/menu or lookup-surface carve-outs (both are on-record narrower: bolding a mode word like **Read:**, not every list item's own lead). Each individual bold span is within the ≲5-word handle cap, so this is a budget violation (>1 bolded element per slide), not a handle-vs-sentence violation. Harm is mildly present (bold no longer distinguishes a single handle from the rest) but the pattern is a corpus-wide, deliberate LO/norms convention, so filing as non-blocking per the rule's own blocking partition.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If this is meant to be exempt (LO/checklist items functioning as named handles), say so in the maintainer block per rule 9's own carve-out language rather than leaving it silently outside all three stated exemptions.
